**DigitAI | Kuala Lumpur | Full-time, on site | RM9,000 to RM12,000**

**AI Automation Engineer**

Join DigitAI as our first engineering hire and build the systems the other companies in our ecosystem run on. We are looking for an AI Automation Engineer to design, ship and own the AI agents, automations and internal tools that replace manual work across those companies, and then turn the best of them into products other businesses pay to use. You will report directly to the CEO.

**The role in short:**

This is a build role, and you are the one building it.

There is no engineering team above you to inherit patterns from and no legacy system to maintain. You will pick up a defined stack, a queue of real problems across finance, marketing, business development and web, and direct daily access to the CEO to decide what gets built and in what order.

We care about speed more than most places say they do. Not hours logged, and not shortcuts. What we mean is that the distance between a decision and a shipped thing should be days, not quarters. There is no committee, no approval chain, and no quarterly planning cycle standing between you and production. You will get an answer the same day and ship the same week, and the standard for quality does not move to make that possible. Working in focused, short cycles is how it gets done, not something we sacrifice to get there.

Your first year is about shipping automations that people actually use, proving which of them are good enough to lease externally, and leaving behind documentation and operational discipline good enough that a second engineer can join without archaeology.

If you want a seat where the architecture is settled and the job is to add features to it, this is not that role. If you have wanted to design an AI-first system properly, from the data layer to the agent layer to the dashboard, and be accountable for whether it works, it is.

**As our AI Automation Engineer, you will be responsible for:**

**1) Building and shipping AI agents and automations.**

* Build agents and multi-step automations that replace manual work across finance, marketing, business development and web.
* Wire third-party APIs and large language models into workflows that run in production, not in a demonstration.
* Ship in weeks, not quarters. Get something real in front of a real user early, then improve it against what they actually do with it.
* Work directly with the CEO, who has built and run multiple award-winning companies across several industries over 17 years. One decision maker, no committee. Your job includes challenging the brief where the brief is wrong, and you will get a straight answer either way, quickly.

**2) Productising what works.**

* Take internal tools that have proven themselves and turn them into something that can be leased to other businesses.
* Build for a second user from the start: configuration, tenancy, onboarding and support paths, not a one-off script with your name on it.

**3) Owning what you build, end to end.**

* Design it, ship it, deploy it, monitor it, and keep it running.
* Work across a Next.js, Tailwind, Supabase and Vercel stack, with Python for data, numerical work, integrations and scraping.
* Build reliable scheduled and multi-step workflows that fail loudly rather than silently.

**4) Reliability, evaluation and documentation.**

* Know whether your systems are producing correct output, and be able to prove it. Evaluating non-deterministic systems is part of the job, not an afterthought.
* Carry the standards our ecosystem already runs on: audit logs, soft deletes, and no single-person deploy path. These are not negotiable for anything touching money or leased to a client.
* Write documentation another engineer can follow. This is a deliverable of the role, not a hope.

**Requirements**

* Minimum 4 years building and shipping production software. Not prototypes, not coursework.
* Strong in both TypeScript and Python. This one is not negotiable, because the work spans a JavaScript application layer and a Python data and automation layer.
* You have built something with large language models that goes beyond a single prompt and response: an agent, a multi-step workflow, something that uses tools or makes decisions. And you can tell us how you knew it was actually working.
* Comfortable with Postgres or Supabase.
* You have shipped things people used, and you can show them.
* You move fast without being careless, and you can tell the difference between the two.
* You reason from first principles, defend your choices with logic, and change your mind when the evidence changes.
* You write documentation other people can follow.

**What this role is not.**

We are not hiring for model training, fine-tuning or deep learning research. No PyTorch or TensorFlow required. If that is the work you want, this seat will disappoint you, and we would rather say so here than at the offer stage.

**Extra credits if you:**

* Have done browser automation and scraping, particularly with Playwright.
* Have used workflow, queue or durable execution tooling.
* Have productised or leased software you built yourself.
* Have front-end polish, particularly with Tailwind.
* Have worked on finance systems or data pipelines.

**What will you be joining?**

We are a company within a bigger ecosystem: a group of award-winning companies operating across Malaysia, Singapore and Indonesia, in industries including esports, event organising, digital marketing, licensed private equity and quantitative trading.

DigitAI is the newest of them, and this is a new function. We build artificial intelligence systems that replace manual work. Every agent, automation and tool we make goes to work inside the ecosystem, where we carry the cost of it being wrong.

That ecosystem is why this is not a typical early-stage engineering job. You get real operations to build against from day one, real data, real users who will tell you within the hour when something does not work, and the resources of an established organisation behind a small team.

If you are looking to take your career to the next height, we will provide the opportunities and resources to help you hone your abilities and develop new skills, so long as you are eager and hungry to learn.

**What kind of culture should I expect?**

* The average age of our organisation is approximately 28 years old, with a strong desire for growth and learning.
* A fun and enjoyable working environment that values humility, a positive attitude, teamwork and creativity.
* Our team is comfortable being called out if something does not meet standards, with little offence taken personally.
* Our progressive management initiates self-evaluation exercises, culture days, team alignment sessions and town halls.
* We appreciate guidance and mentorship, and actively foster a supportive environment for our team to grow and develop their skills and expertise.
* We enjoy pantry restocks, regular team-building activities and company trips, amongst others.

**What should I expect from work?**

* You will be working directly with our CEO, who will be personally involved in mentoring and guiding you. For this role that access is daily, not quarterly, and it covers the business side as much as the technical. Ask anyone who has worked closely with the CEO, from any industry, profession or level of seniority, and you will hear the same thing: the learning curve is steep, and it does not flatten.
* You will be given real responsibility and real autonomy from day one, and you will own what you build rather than take tickets from someone else.
* A pace that will not suit everyone. We would rather ship, watch it fail somewhere, and fix it in the same week than spend a quarter making sure it cannot.
* A significant budget for experimentation, tooling and learning. You will not be asked to itemise it, but you will be asked to make the case for it, and a good case gets an answer the same day.
* A results-linked bonus tied to what you ship, whether it gets adopted, and what it earns.
* A fast growth path. Scope and band expand quickly for the right person, and the second engineer will be hired underneath what you have built.

**Being honest about how we work:**
this is the first engineering hire in a fast-moving company. We move quickly, we work hard, and there will be times when the work happens at unusual hours. We would rather tell you that now than have you discover it in month two.

**Salary:**

RM9,000 to RM12,000 per month; we set the level by what you can demonstrate, not by years served.

**Location:**

Fully on site. We are currently located in Bukit Tunku, Kuala Lumpur, and will be moving to Pavilion Damansara Heights Corporate Tower shortly.

**How to apply:**

Send your curriculum vitae together with links to two or three things you have shipped. A repository, a live product, or a short written description if the work is under a non-disclosure agreement. Tell us what your specific contribution was on each.

**Note**
: We receive more than 1,000 curricula vitae across our companies on a monthly basis and we might potentially miss out on some good candidates. If you think that you fit into the role described, please resubmit your application with us. We celebrate persistence!

Seniority Level: Mid-Senior level

Data & Platform Collaboration
  
  

* Work with data engineers to define semantic contracts, metric definitions and approved analytical functions that AI features can rely on.
* Work with full-stack engineers to integrate AI features into web applications, dashboards and workflow screens.
* Contribute to the Group's responsible AI standards, including documentation of model cards, intended use, known limitations and review history.

Stakeholder Engagement
  
  

* Explain model behaviour, limitations and risk controls to non-technical stakeholders — including partners, compliance and risk functions.
* Translate business questions into measurable AI capabilities with defined inputs, outputs and evaluation criteria.
* Provide pragmatic guidance on where AI is and is not the right tool, including when conventional analytics or process automation would be safer or more effective.

**Required Experience & Skills**

* 3–5+ years applying AI, ML or data science techniques in production or business-critical environments.
* Strong Python experience, including pandas and modern ML/AI libraries.
* Experience with LLM application development, including tool calling, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), evals, prompt management or agent-style workflows.
* Experience with SQL, analytical datasets and governed data access patterns.
* Familiarity with model monitoring, experiment tracking, model registry or broader MLOps practices.
* Understanding of privacy, security, audit logging and data minimisation in AI systems.
* Ability to translate business questions into measurable AI capabilities and clearly explain limitations to non-specialists.

Desirable Experience
  
  

* Experience with document intelligence, NLP, financial data, forecasting or classification problems.
* Exposure to regulated environments (financial services, legal, audit) and an appreciation of the additional controls this demand.
* Experience with vector databases, semantic search, or hybrid retrieval architectures.
* Familiarity with OpenRouter, Azure AI services, Azure OpenAI, or comparable enterprise AI tooling.
* Experience contributing to responsible AI policies, AI risk assessments, or model governance forums.

Success Measures
  
  

* User impact: AI features measurably improve user productivity without weakening access control or auditability.
* Grounding: AI answers are grounded in approved data sources and tested against known scenarios — hallucinations on material questions are caught before release, not after.
* Regression control: Evals reliably catch regressions in tenancy, permissions, financial accuracy and response quality before features are promoted.
* Transparency: Model and tool usage, failures and limitations are visible through telemetry and reviewed regularly by engineering and compliance.
* Defensibility: AI features can be explained, evidenced and defended to internal audit and, where relevant, external regulators.

Working Environment
  
  

* Reporting line: Group Technology leadership, working day-to-day within a cross-functional product squad (engineering, data, AI, design, product).

Governance, Security & Compliance Expectations
  
  
Every engineer in Group Technology is expected to treat the following as non-negotiable foundations, not optional extras:
  
  

* Confidentiality: Client, matter, and case data is highly sensitive. Need-to-know access is the default; broad access is the exception and must be justified.
* Security by design: Threat modelling, secure defaults, secrets management, dependency scanning and least-privilege access are built into features from day one.
* Responsible AI: Where AI is used, model behaviour, prompts, tools and data access are versioned, evaluated and monitored. Human oversight is preserved for material decisions.
* Regulatory awareness: For features touching FCA-regulated entities (e.g. Pareto, Luna), additional controls apply around record-keeping, client communications and data handling. Engineers are expected to flag uncertainty early.
* Data protection: UK GDPR and Group data protection standards apply across all subsidiaries; data minimisation, lawful basis and retention controls are part of normal design.

Development & Progression

Person Specification
